speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Patient
text: nt appears anxious. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising, as Multiple Sclerosis typically does not cause joint swelling or urinary pain; could you confirm if you have had any recent episodes of fever, skin rashes, or eye redness? I have already requested a Urinalysis and Serum Uric Acid to check for gout or infection.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported. Social history: Sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The combination of urethritis (pain with urination), arthritis (knee and ankle), and the specific social history of multiple sexual partners without consistent protection is classic for this condition, which can also present with conjunctivitis or keratitis. I recommend you return to your physician to review the urinalysis results, start antibiotic treatment for the underlying infection, and discuss joint management.
